title: Mahāpadāna / Mahāvadāna multi-witness vertical slice
scope: Initial model-reviewed alignment across Pāli DN 14, Chinese DA 1 and EA 48.4, and Sanskrit SF 36.
epistemic_policy: These are model-reviewed source-unit correspondences for research triage. They preserve recension differences and editorial reconstruction. None is human-established.

members.notes: Opening formula and Jetavana setting; additionally specifies karerikuṭikā.
Opening formula plus Śrāvastī/Jetavana setting.
Opening formula plus Śrāvastī/Jetavana/Anāthapiṇḍada setting.
Opening formula and setting; several letters in the edition are supplied.

variants.statement: The witnesses share the opening and Jetavana setting, but differ in the granularity and wording of the immediate residence detail.

review.notes: Strong formulaic and narrative correspondence. No claim of verbal identity.

members.notes: The discussion is summarized as concerning pubbenivāsa, without the detailed question found in the other recensions.

Detailed discussion of past Buddhas and whether the Tathāgata knows through understanding 法性 or information from devas; the Chinese term is preserved without asserting one-to-one equivalence with Sanskrit dharmadhātu.

Detailed discussion of past Buddhas and the 法處/deva question in this opening block; the later repeated report uses 法界. These Chinese terms are preserved rather than normalized into a single Sanskrit equivalent.
Expands the discussion into knowledge of past Buddhas, their qualities, and the dharmadhātu versus deva-report question.

variants.statement: SF 36, DA 1, and EA 48.4 preserve an expanded discussion about knowledge of past Buddhas and a dharmadhātu/deva-report question; DN 14 at this point gives only the shorter pubbenivāsa topic.

SF 36 explicitly has dharmadhātu, DA 1 has 法性, and EA 48.4 has 法處 in the opening discussion (with 法界 in the later repeated report). The witnesses share an analogous question frame about how the Tathāgata knows past Buddhas, but this alignment does not assert that these terms are lexically or doctrinally identical.

review.notes: Accepted as partial overlap because the Pāli unit is materially shorter than the Sanskrit and Chinese passages. The dharmadhātu / 法性 / 法處 wording is kept witness-specific; lexical equivalence is deliberately left unasserted.

members.notes: Buddha hears with purified divine ear, approaches, sits, and asks what the monks were discussing.
Hearing/approach and question are split across two blocks.
Hearing, approach, sitting in the middle, and question are compressed into one block.
Marks the unfinished discussion, then divine-ear hearing/approach, then the Buddha's question.

variants.statement: The same narrative sequence is divided differently: one Pāli paragraph, two DA blocks, one EA block, and three Sanskrit paragraphs.

review.notes: Strong narrative and lexical correspondence despite differing segmentation.

members.notes: Repeats only the abbreviated pubbenivāsa topic.
Says the monks answered fully, but does not repeat the detailed content in this block.
Repeats the expanded discussion and dharmadhātu/deva question.
Repeats the expanded discussion and dharmadhātu/deva question in detail.

variants.statement: DA 1 replaces the repeated speech with a narrative statement that the monks answered fully; DN 14 repeats only the short topic, while EA 48.4 and SF 36 repeat the expanded question.

review.notes: Alignment is structural rather than full verbal correspondence.

members.notes: Lists Vipassī through the present Buddha with 91/31-kalpa chronology.
Prose list followed by verse restatement.
Prose list and verse restatement; the verse-introduction block is excluded as framing.
Prose list and damaged/reconstructed verse section; supplied text remains explicit in edition_text.

variants.statement: DA 1, EA 48.4, and SF 36 preserve a prose chronology followed by a verse restatement in the selected units, while the selected Pāli member is prose only. The Sanskrit verse is substantially fragmentary and editorially supplied.

review.notes: Strong agreement in sequence and chronology; names appear in language-specific forms.

members.notes: 80k/70k/60k/40k/30k/20k; present lifespan about 100 years.

Both prose and verse are framed as 人壽, the human lifespan in the time of each Buddha, rather than explicitly as the Buddha's own lifespan. Prose gives 80k/70k/60k/40k/30k/20k; the verse gives Vipassī 84k.
Prose gives 84k/70k/60k/50k/40k/20k; present maximum 100.
Prose gives 80k/70k/60k/40k/30k/20k; the verse is fragmentary/supplied in places.

variants.statement: DN 14 and SF 36 prose explicitly give Buddha lifespans of 80k/70k/60k/40k/30k/20k; EA 48.4 explicitly gives Tathāgata lifespans of 84k/70k/60k/50k/40k/20k. DA 1 gives human lifespan (人壽) in each Buddha's era: prose 80k/70k/60k/40k/30k/20k, while its verse changes Vipassī-era human lifespan to 84k. The numerical resemblance is preserved without equating these differently framed subjects.
DA 1 and SF 36 preserve prose plus verse forms for this list, while the selected Pāli unit is prose and the selected EA member uses the prose list only.

DA 1 frames the quantities as human lifespan (人壽) in each Buddha's era, whereas DN 14 and SF 36 frame them as the Buddha's lifespan and EA 48.4 as the Tathāgata's lifespan. This semantic subject difference must not be normalized away.

review.notes: The four witnesses place comparable numerical lists at the same narrative locus, but DA 1 frames the values as human lifespan (人壽) in each Buddha's era while DN 14 and SF 36 frame Buddha lifespans and EA 48.4 frames Tathāgata lifespans. The row is therefore classified conservatively as structural correspondence rather than a full textual parallel.

members.notes: First three and the present Buddha are kṣatriya; the middle three are brāhmaṇa.
Same caste pattern, with clan-name information embedded in the same prose block.
Same caste pattern in a dedicated prose block.
Same caste pattern; all three Sanskrit leaf segments contain supplied reconstruction.

variants.statement: DA 1 combines caste and clan-name information in the same prose block, while the selected Pāli, EA 48.4, and SF 36 units here isolate the caste pattern more cleanly.

review.notes: The caste sequence is stable across the selected witnesses; DA 1 packages extra clan information into the same block.

members.notes: Koṇḍañña for the first three, Kassapa for the middle three, Gotama for the present Buddha.
Clan names appear in the same prose block as caste.

EA preserves two complete nearby clan-name sequences that are internally incompatible: b0015 gives Gotama for the first three, Kassapa for the middle three, and Gotama for the present Buddha; b0018 gives 拘鄰若 for the first three, 婆羅墮 for the middle three, and 拘鄰若 for the present Buddha.
The edited source unit explicitly states that the Sanskrit text is completely lost under the Family Name subsection.

variants.statement: SF 36 has no surviving Sanskrit wording for the Family Name subsection in the selected edition; the source unit explicitly marks the text as completely lost.

EA 48.4 preserves two complete nearby clan-name sequences that disagree with one another, while the selected Pāli and DA 1 prose present one main sequence each. The internal EA disagreement is retained rather than reconciled.

EA 48.4 b0015 reads the first three Buddhas as Gotama and the middle three as Kassapa (with present Gotama), while b0018 reads the first three as 拘鄰若 and the middle three as 婆羅墮 (with present 拘鄰若). These are incompatible clan-name series within the same recension and are not harmonized.

review.notes: Recension divergence is assessed from the surviving Pāli, DA 1, and EA 48.4 wording. SF 36 contributes only an explicit Family Name loss locus and is not treated as surviving textual evidence for the relation.
